jobs.occupation: Product Owner - Shape the Future of Industrial Ice Cream Filling
jobs.description:
At Gram Equipment, we develop the technology behind ice cream products enjoyed by people around the world.

As a global provider of equipment and complete production solutions for the ice cream industry, we combine more than a century of experience with innovation, technical expertise and close customer collaboration. Our filling solutions help customers produce cups, cones, tubs and other filled products efficiently, reliably and at high quality.

We are now looking for a Product Owner to help develop and strengthen our filling product portfolio with emphasis on the Flexline product.
Your Role
As Product Owner – Flexline, you will take technical ownership of our filling product portfolio and play a central role in its continued development.

You will connect customer requirements, market opportunities and operational experience with engineering and product development. Working closely with Product Management, Engineering, Automation, Sales, Projects, Production and Service, you will ensure that our filling solutions remain competitive, reliable and aligned with customer needs.

You will maintain the product roadmap, prioritize improvements and support projects throughout the value chain—from quotation and technical clarification to production, commissioning and lifecycle support.

The role does not include direct personnel responsibility. Your influence comes through your product expertise, judgment and ability to create alignment across functions.
Key ResponsibilitiesProduct Ownership and Roadmap
• Maintain and develop the roadmap for Gram Equipment’s filling product portfolio.
• Identify and prioritize product improvements based on customer needs, field experience, market developments and business priorities.
• Define product requirements and help translate strategic priorities into concrete development activities.
• Monitor competitor technologies and identify relevant performance or technology gaps.
• Maintain product standards and ensure that approved improvements are implemented and sustained.Technical and Cross-Functional Execution
• Support project reviews, design approvals, technical clarifications and decisions concerning product interfaces.
• Ensure that project-specific solutions remain aligned with product standards, technical feasibility, safety, cost and delivery requirements.
• Coordinate closely with mechanical engineering, automation, production, assembly and project management.
• Support testing, validation and commissioning and use the resulting learning to improve the product portfolio.
• Contribute to the resolution of complex technical and field-performance issues.Commercial and Customer Support
• Support Sales and Internal Sales with quotations, equipment selection, configurations and technical customer dialogue.
• Participate in customer meetings and communicate product capabilities, options and technical limitations clearly.
• Balance filling performance, customer value, reliability, standardization and commercial competitiveness.
• Develop an understanding of customer applications and production requirements and use this insight to strengthen future solutions.Product Lifecycle Management
• Maintain relevant product specifications, documentation, equipment structures and product data.
• Coordinate product changes and ensure that decisions are properly documented, released and communicated.
• Support standardization and lifecycle management across existing and future filling platforms.
• Ensure that products comply with relevant food-safety, hygienic-design, machine-safety and regulatory requirements.Your Profile
We are looking for someone who combines strong technical understanding with product ownership, commercial awareness and an interest in working across the organization.

You bring:

• A relevant technical education, preferably within mechanical engineering, process technology, production engineering or a comparable field.
• Experience with product ownership, product development, mechanical engineering or technical project execution within industrial machinery or a related industry.
• A good understanding of mechanical equipment, machine interfaces and the interaction between mechanics and automation.
• Experience with hygienic equipment, food production or filling and dosing technology is an advantage.
• The ability to understand customer applications and translate technical and commercial needs into product requirements and practical solutions.
• A structured approach to product roadmaps, technical decisions, documentation and follow-up.
• Commercial awareness and an understanding of how product decisions influence customer value, project performance and lifecycle cost.
• Strong collaboration and communication skills and the ability to influence decisions without formal authority.
• Good written and spoken English.
Experience with Inventor, Vault, AutoCAD, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central or comparable engineering and ERP systems would be an advantage.

Above all, you are curious about how products perform in real customer environments. You enjoy developing technical knowledge, asking questions and bringing people together around solutions that work across the full value chain.
What We Offer
• A central role with genuine influence on the future direction of Gram Equipment’s filling portfolio with emphasis on the Flexline product.
• The opportunity to combine technology, customer insight, commercial understanding and product development.
• Close cooperation with experienced specialists across Engineering, Automation, Sales, Production, Projects and Service.
• An international working environment with customers and colleagues across global markets.
• Opportunities for professional development and increasing product responsibility.
• An informal and collaborative workplace where knowledge sharing and practical improvement are valued.
• Competitive employment conditions aligned with your experience and qualifications.
The position is based at our headquarters in Kolding, Denmark. You should expect approximately 0–30 travel days per year, primarily for customer meetings, technical clarification, commissioning support and product validation.

**Job Description

**In Credit Risk Model Validation (CRMV), we are reimagining model risk management across Danske Bank, moving from manual data wrangling, ad hoc scripts, and copied notebooks towards an industrialised, reproducible, AI-accelerated quantitative engineering ecosystem.

To realise this vision, we are looking for a Senior Model Validation Quant who bridges quantitative model validation and software and infrastructure engineering. You will combine strong quantitative skills with sound engineering practices to validate models, build our core validation software, and configure modern cloud workflows.

Enabling the team to perform high-quality, repeatable validations is as important as running them yourself. Your initial focus will be roughly 70% direct model validation and 30% tooling and infrastructure engineering, adapting as our platform and automation mature.

You will join a skilled, collaborative, forward-thinking team of risk professionals migrating to GitHub Enterprise Cloud and Databricks, building modular internal Python packages, configuring Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) and GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows, and using GitHub Copilot as a daily engineering partner.

**What you will be doing:

**

• Perform and lead model validations: independently validate credit risk models (e.g. PD, LGD, CF, and IFRS 9), assessing conceptual soundness, statistical performance, and model limitations.

• Build and evolve validation software: design, implement, and maintain core Python packages and shared libraries that translate quantitative methodologies into clean, parameter-driven, testable tools.

• Enable the department: create tools and automated templates that help fellow validators run analyses, generate standard evidence bundles, and produce publication-ready PDF reports with minimal manual effort.

• Design modern workflows and infrastructure: set up and manage GitHub Actions workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) for automated, audit-ready execution across environments.

• Integrate AI-assisted engineering: use GitHub Copilot extensively each day to accelerate code delivery, write comprehensive test suites, and modernise legacy codebases.

• Promote engineering excellence: promote sound version control practices, structured code reviews, and reproducible analyses across the team.

• Engage key stakeholders: clearly and persuasively present technical architectures, quantitative findings, and validation conclusions to model developers, risk leaders, and regulatory counterparts.

**About you:

**

• Quantitative grounding: you have an MSc or PhD, or equivalent practical experience, in a quantitative discipline (e.g. mathematics, statistics, computer science, physics, quantitative finance, data science, or engineering).

• Strong coding practices: you have solid practical experience writing clean, modular Python and SQL code.

• Collaborative version control (Git is essential): you are confident with Git branching strategies, pull requests, automated checks, and collaborative code reviews.

• Infrastructure and automation mindset: you have practical experience with, or a strong interest in learning, platforms such as Databricks (including DABs) and GitHub Actions.

• Enthusiasm for AI tooling: you are keen to use GitHub Copilot daily to enhance your workflow. Prior experience is a plus, but curiosity and openness to AI-assisted coding matter most.

• Bridge-builder mindset: you enjoy combining quantitative modelling with software engineering and switching between building infrastructure and exploring model mechanics.

• Clear communicator: you communicate clearly and warmly in English, translating technical and mathematical nuances into accessible insights for colleagues with varied backgrounds.

**What we offer you:

**This position can be located both in Denmark and Lithuania. If the position is located in Lithuania, the salary range will be from 3280 EUR to 4920 EUR gross (based on your competencies relevant for the job) and your contractual job title will be Risk Methodology & Model Validation.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**Does this sound like the opportunity you have been looking for? We would like to hear from you.

If you have any questions, please contact Morten Gadegaard Jørgensen mojrg@danskebank.dk

Are you a hands-on, security focused engineer ready to help build a technical security foundation? If you thrive on turning compliance frameworks into real-world technical control while staying closely connected to daily operations, this job is for you.

Working closely with our Head of IT and Security, you will turn our ISMS (ISO/IEC 27001, NIS2, and the EU AI Act) into operating technical reality by designing, implementing, and operating the controls, tooling, and secure configurations that protect Space Inventor across our Corporate, Missions, and SatOPS zones. This is a role focused on establishing new capabilities rather than maintaining an existing setup. Alongside hands-on security engineering, you will co-own and deliver day-to-day IT support, keeping you grounded in user needs and the operational reality of our environment.

Given Space Inventors work you must be eligible for a Danish Personnel Security Clearance.

The job is located in Aalborg, Denmark.

Your Responsibilities

• Core Security & Tooling: Design, implement, and operate core security controls and tooling (EDR, logging/SIEM, vulnerability management, email, and endpoint security).

• Identity & Access Management: Build and harden the identity foundation (Entra ID security, MFA, Conditional Access, PAM, Windows LAPS, and access governance).

• Hardening & Infrastructure: Establish endpoint and server hardening baselines (CIS benchmarks) enforced via Intune; support secure design for infrastructure rebuilds and Entra ID/M365 migrations.

• Network & Zone Security: Implement network security and segmentation across our three zones (Corporate, Missions, SatOPS), including the overlay for OT and the SatOPS ground segment.

• Vulnerability Management & Incident Response: Scan, prioritize, remediate, and verify vulnerabilities; build detection, alerting, playbooks, and hands-on investigation/recovery.

• Automation & Architecture: Automate security operations via PowerShell/scripting; contribute to technical roadmaps, document controls, and serve as a technical security resource.

• Compliance & Governance: Implement technical controls behind the Statement of Applicability and produce evidence for ISO 27001 certification and NIS2 compliance.

• IT Operations & Support: Co-own and deliver day-to-day service desk support, troubleshooting endpoint/user issues, Microsoft 365, onboarding/offboarding, and hardware/AV lifecycles.

Qualifications

Experience: 3 to 6 years of hands-on experience in IT security engineering or SecOps specifically building or maturing controls from scratch combined with solid IT support experience. Experience from regulated, manufacturing, critical-infrastructure, or OT environments is an advantage (space experience is not required).

Technical Proficiencies:

• Hands-on security engineering across endpoints, identity, cloud, and networks.

• Microsoft security stack: Entra ID, Conditional Access, Intune, M365 security, Defender (EDR), and ideally Sentinel or a comparable SIEM.

• Hardening baselines (CIS), patch management, and vulnerability scanning.

• Network security: Firewalls, segmentation, VPNs, and traffic monitoring.

• Scripting and automation with PowerShell.

• Incident response, triage, and log analysis.

Standards & Compliance: Solid working knowledge of ISO/IEC 27001 and NIS2 requirements; awareness of OT / IEC 62443 is a strong plus.

Education & Certifications: Degree in IT/cybersecurity or equivalent proven experience. Relevant certifications (e.g., Microsoft SC-200/AZ-500/SC-100, CompTIA Security+/CySA+, or GIAC GSEC/GCIH) are an advantage.

Personal Attributes: A builder mindset with strong initiative; pragmatic and risk-oriented; structured with audit-ready documentation; and a clear, discreet communicator who collaborates well across technical and non-technical teams.

What We Offer

• A full-time role with exposure to a variety of disciplines within space technology.

• A position in an exciting, rapidly growing industry with significant international reach.

• A chance to shape your role and responsibilities within a growing company.

• Great colleagues and several social events each year.

• Health insurance and additional employee benefits.

• Competitive salary and good working conditions.

How to Apply

If you’re ready to take your career to the next level, apply by submitting your CV and application. If you have any questions about the position, feel free to contact us via jobs@space-inventor.com, and we’ll get back to you as soon as possible.

Interviews are held continuously until the right candidate is found.

Start date to be agreed, but preferably with start-up as soon as possible.

We look forward to receiving your application.

We are looking for a Software Engineer who wants to build and ship new features that quickly reach customers, on top of an engine that already runs at scale. You join our platform team, which owns several live domains that our customers depend on every day. The foundations are solid and well maintained, so your time goes into new use cases and features rather than firefighting. Whether you have a couple of years of experience or a few more, we would like to see your application.

**What's in it for you?

**

• Hear directly from the people using what you build. Customer feedback feeds straight back into the roadmap, and you work on features and product decisions that matter to end users.

• Build on a system with real scale behind it. The event system spans 8 domains, exposes 20+ event types as webhooks, and powers 10 configurable alert types for our end users - currently ~20k active configurations triggering ~200k events every weekday. The team owns 8+ public APIs end to end, crucial for customers' day-to-day business.

• Learn from experts who share. You’ll join a talkative team of experienced domain experts who love discussing technical topics.

• Grow with support. Scoped, well-defined assignments to start, senior colleagues pairing and reviewing your work, and shared ownership of keeping things running.

• See your work ship. We favour small, frequent releases over long project cycles, so what you build lands in production fast.

**Who are you ideally?

**You are a backend developer with strong Java skills who is at home on live production systems.

• Hands-on experience with Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, and REST APIs, in particular building and running your own services in a modern cloud-based microservice and event-driven architecture.

• You are comfortable working on live production systems with high data volumes and migration paths, keeping quality, observability, reliability, and performance in mind.

• You enjoy talking tech: you like discussing technical topics widely, learning, and listening in on topics not always directly related to your own tasks.

• You are motivated by incremental, high-quality delivery on products that are already live, bringing a fresh perspective that helps rework existing infrastructure where it is holding us back, and you treat the tools already in our platform as solid building blocks.

• Nice to have: Flink and stateful processing (or the willingness to learn it, since it is widely used here), relational databases, and Grafana and Prometheus, our “bread and butter”.

You embrace AI as part of how you engineer. From prototyping through to production, you use AI tools as an integrated part of your workflow, not as a shortcut but as a force multiplier. That said, this isn't the main thing we're hiring for: curiosity and a willingness to use it well matter more than deep prior experience.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries, this is what we're looking for ideally. If you're excited about this role but your background doesn't align perfectly with every point above, we encourage you to apply.

**Primary Responsibilities

**

• Improve, extend and run the live domains our team owns, including telemetry storage and APIs, the event system, and the alerting engine, without disrupting production.

• Build and run your own services, with migration paths when architecture or data formats need to change.

• Work closely with the internal teams building products on top of the platform you help shape.

• Keep the platform reliable and observable at high data volumes.

****Our hiring process

****Don’t waste your time writing the perfect cover letter. We want you to create an impact that matters - and that’s not in the cover letter.

• Initial phone conversation with a colleague from our P&T team.

• Virtual meet and greet with your potential new leader and someone from the team, so you’ll get to know the role and team better.

• Assignment-specific interview with the hiring manager and a lead engineer from the team. We want to give you a real insight into the work. You’ll receive a case to prepare ahead of the interview and present to relevant colleagues - people you’ll also work closely with in the role.

• If needed, we will obtain references from former employers and conduct background checks at relevant levels.

• Offer presentation and walk-through.

Help us evolve the technical foundation for digital manufacturing at VELUX. You will enable development teams to build manufacturing applications through reliable connectivity, standardised shop floor data and reusable platform services.

Meet your future team

As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will provide day-to-day technical leadership across the engineering group. Working closely with senior IIoT platform engineers, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders, you will coordinate decisions, coach engineers and help move delivery forward. The role has no formal people-management responsibility.

What We Offer

This role combines contributing to the shared IIoT platform’s technical direction with direct engineering work. You will lead day-to-day technical direction and engineering execution, contributing to design, development, testing, reviews and complex problem-solving. You will turn product priorities into a coherent platform roadmap, engineering practices and clear guardrails.

Act as the first technical escalation point. Guide external engineering contributions so standards, knowledge and lifecycle accountability remain within the team. You bring 7+ years of relevant experience in software, platform or integration engineering, including technical leadership in an industrial IT/OT or digital manufacturing environment. You understand both manufacturing-domain needs and Unified Namespace. You use that understanding to make technical choices that work for platform users and the engineering team.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Bring practical knowledge across industrial connectivity and edge technologies, including MQTT, edge runtimes and container orchestration. You also understand industrial data contracts, observability or SRE practices, and OT cyber security.

• Can translate product priorities into an actionable platform roadmap, technical guardrails and engineering practices.

• Can make practical technical design decisions while involving engineers and relevant stakeholders in finding workable solutions.

• Use effective coaching, facilitation, collaboration and communication skills across engineers, product roles, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders.

• Apply a platform mindset focused on reuse, self-service, consumer enablement, operational excellence and long-term maintainability.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is an advanced systems and industrialization company developing integrated technology platforms for demanding aerospace, security, and mission-critical applications. Its mission is to transform operationally validated technologies into scalable, ready-to-deploy systems by combining advanced engineering, industrial partnerships, and strong governance.

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development. The site will build core capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

One of the initial focus areas will be the development of integrated antenna and RF front-end subsystems for high-performance direction finding systems in ELINT applications. The work will cover system and RF architecture, UWB antenna systems, RF receiver front-end hardware, OTA characterization and calibration, mechanical integration, and preparation for production and field deployment. Initial developments will target ground and airborne platforms, with the same core technologies later evolving toward aerospace and satellite applications.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and international deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior Systems Engineer, RF Systems to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s systems-engineering capability for advanced RF and signal-intelligence products.

Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is looking for a full-time Data manager to work at the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT).

Land-CRAFT addresses three of our major societal challenges - food security, climate change, and loss of biodiversity. With Center partners from University of Copenhagen, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Germany), and Colorado State University (USA), we bring together expertise in climate impact research, landscape analyses, biogeochemistry, agronomy, biology, and geography to develop solution – oriented research that extends across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Established in June 2022, Land-CRAFT has built a dynamic team to undertake both fundamental and applied research aimed to reduce the environmental impact of agricultural systems, specifically regarding greenhouse gas emissions. To reach our goals, we are using a combination of empirical, field-based approaches, digital technologies, including modelling and remote sensing, while closely interacting with stakeholders. The position we advertise here is aimed at supporting these activities with respect to data management. The new employee will become part of a support team with complementary skills and work collaboratively in an active and international research environment with diverse projects and people across Department of Agroecology.

The position is available from 1st March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The duration of the position is 3 years.

Responsibilities and tasks
Your main role as part of the support team at Land-CRAFT will be to support research activities of the staff and research students (at BSc, MSc, and PhD levels) in data management, analysis and statistics. This will include maintaining and supplementing relational databases used for process-based modelling and geospatial data analyses. Main responsibilities and tasks include:

• 
Organize, archive, and document data collected by the Land-CRAFT team, including with appropriate metadata protocols

• 
Manage data transfer/sharing among Center partners and external collaborators following FAIR data principles, AU rules and regulations, and GDPR rules

• 
Manage user access and permissions within the AU File system and user data on a computational server

• 
Create and manage a database on research outputs from the Center, including e.g., publications, citations and other reports, to facilitate website updates, annual reports, and other communication platforms, as well as managing the Zenodo community

• 
Support staff and students with statistical and geospatial analyses (e.g. in R and Python)

• 
Support/manage data collection pipeline from instruments in the lab & field (including visualisation of data in e.g. Origin)

• 
Establish, maintain, and refine documentation regarding all data-related protocols (e.g. data policy, data management plans, etc.)

• 
Coordinating data management across the Department of Agroecology (about 20 % of time) in collaboration with the department’s data steward

Your profile
As a member of the Land-Craft support team, we expect you to plan and perform your tasks independently and initiate frequent feedback and communication with Land CRAFT researchers and students. The position requires that you can communicate with and support students and scientists from BSc to Professor levels, including attention to detail and quality (QA/QC) and an affinity for knowledge-sharing, e.g., in working with students as they learn to manage their own data. You have a high proficiency in English, are culturally sensitive, and can work in a large group of diverse colleagues and students. At Land-CRAFT we emphasize good relationships among colleagues and students. It is therefore important that you have a positive and open personality, stay engaged with emerging challenges and opportunities, and are ready to support colleagues when needed.

Qualifications

• 
MSc in data science, agroecology, geoscience, biology, ecology, environmental science, mathematics, geography (or related fields)

• 
Knowledge and understanding of data management plans, metadata systems, archiving practices

• 
Experience in statistical analysis; knowledge of R or Python, as well as visualisation platforms

• 
Good collaboration and communications skills across different groups of employees,

• 
High level of English proficiency and cultural sensitivity

• 
Interest in and willingness to acquire general knowledge about Land-CRAFT’s research areas

• 
Familiarity with the Danish administrative structures or Danish language.

Workplace
The place of work is Aarhus University, Ole Worms Alle 3, DK-8000 Aarhus C. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

Who we are
At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.
We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer

• 
A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.

• 
An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.

• 
A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.

• 
An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.

• 
An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.

• 
Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme

Contact information
More information can be obtained from Klaus Butterbach-Bahl (klaus.butterbach bahl@agro.au.dk).

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions..You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8.

jobs.occupation: 4 PhD positions in AI-accelerated development of PFAS-free polymer-based battery materials cells in Self-driving Laboratories - DTU Energy and BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in a career in AI for materials and in accelerating the green transition? If so, we have a number of positions at DTU that might just right for you. 

The four PhD positions at DTU Energy are part of BRIGHT's mission-oriented Novel Biomanufacturing-Enabled Materials research programme, referred to as Mission 1A, which aims to create new classes of PFAS-free functional biomaterials through biotechnology. The mission's current focus are proteinaceous materials with defined composition, programmable chemistry and controlled assembly as sustainable alternatives to persistent fluorinated materials. The scientific scope spans AI-guided protein and peptide design, microbial engineering, non-canonical amino acid biosynthesis and incorporation, cell-free prototyping, fermentation, purification, materials processing, analytical quality control and structure-function characterization. The programme focuses on building an integrated pipeline from molecular design to scalable biomanufacturing and material testing, with explicit attention to manufacturability, cost, sustainability and industrial translation. Batteries provide the first proof-of-concept application, because PFAS-containing materials are currently used in several battery components and because this sector imposes strict requirements for stability, processability and performance. The broader ambition is to establish a versatile biomanufacturing platform for advanced PFAS-free materials with future relevance across energy technologies, coatings, electronics and other high-value applications.

You will work closely with experimental and computational colleagues in BRIGHT and in DTU Energy, as well as with our international collaborators, e.g., on the use cases on advanced battery materials in MaterialsCommons for Europe and on the development of Self-driving Laboratories (SDLs) at the Pioneer Center CAPeX. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
All four positions are centered on the application of novel PFAS-free proteins and polypeptides for applications in sustainable batteries. The design space for finding optimal compositions and synthesis conditions for such polymers for use as, e.g., electrolytes, binders and additives is vast, we are combining self-driving labs, high-throughput machine learning simulations, and agentic AI to transition to digitalization-based autonomous development of high-performing PFAS-free polymer materials for high-performant batteries, i.e., high electrochemical stability, ionic conductivity, coulombic efficiency, and cyclability at a low cost. The positions will target for areas specifically

• Development of automated setup for high-throughput testing of solid polymer electrolytes and binders, e.g., chemical and electrochemical stability, preparation and film casting. 
• Development of automated setup for in situ polymerization of sodium/sodium-based based battery materials
• Self-driving lab modules for autonomous testing of mechanical properties of polymer-based battery materials, interfaces and layers
• Self-driving lab modules for assembly and testing of advanced (e.g., solid-state and anode-less, sodium-based button and coin cell batteries.
Qualifications:

• Good working knowledge of electrochemistry.
• Ability to work independently and plan and carry out complicated tasks.
• Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• A proactive approach to problem-solving, capable of identifying new directions and opportunities within the project.
Desirable Qualifications:

• Experience with self-driving laboratories or building custom experimental hardware

The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). jobs.description:
PhD Project in quantum and nonlinear light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities

  The Niels Bohr Institute
 Faculty of SCIENCE

  University of Copenhagen

  The Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in experimental quantum nanophotonics. The project will be part of the newly established Mikkelsen Photonics group (Quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions), funded by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant.

  Start date is (expected to be) 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  Plasmonic nanocavities confine light to volumes thousands of times below the diffraction limit. In such extreme gaps, emission rates are enhanced by orders of magnitude, strong field gradients appear, and the usual rules of light–matter interaction are rewritten. The project builds on a wafer-scale platform developed in the group, in which colloidal quantum emitters (quantum dots or nanoplatelets) are deterministically placed into thousands of lithographically defined nanocavities with a controlled number of emitters per cavity. The PhD student will develop this platform and use it to study one or more of the following:

   	
• Few-emitter quantum optics: single-photon emission, collective emission, energy transfer and strong coupling with one to a few emitters per cavity. 	
• Cavity-enhanced nonlinear optics: using the extreme field confinement and field gradients of the nanogap to enhance and control nonlinear processes. 	
• Active and electrically tunable nanocavities: integrating functional materials (e.g. ferroelectric or two-dimensional materials) into the gap to switch and tune the emitter–cavity interaction.   The work is primarily experimental and involves nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy (photoluminescence, single-photon and photon-correlation measurements, nonlinear spectroscopy), optoelectronic device characterization and electromagnetic simulations. The specific project will be defined together with the successful candidate.

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of electrical engineering, physics, nanoscience, photonics, materials science or related areas. Applicants can have a background from optoelectronic or nanophotonic devices, semiconductor nanomaterials, optical spectroscopy, nanofabrication or electromagnetic simulation, but we will also consider candidates with different backgrounds. Hands-on experience with optical experiments and an interest in building new experimental setups is an advantage.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?

  The Mikkelsen Photonics group was established at the Niels Bohr Institute in 2026, when Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen moved from Duke University (USA) supported by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant. The group studies quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities and is building a new laboratory combining deeply subwavelength cavities, single-photon spectroscopy, femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy and, in a later phase, cryogenic and high-magnetic-field operation. As one of the first members of the group, the PhD student will have a central role in shaping the experiments and the scientific direction, with close supervision. The group is part of the Quantum Optics and Photonics research area at the Niels Bohr Institute, home to the Center for Hybrid Quantum Networks (Hy-Q), and has access to the nanofabrication facilities at the Niels Bohr Institute and the DTU Nanolab cleanroom.

  The group is a part of the Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen, in the new laboratory and office building of the Niels Bohr Institute.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and new, dedicated optics and nanofabrication facilities.

  Principal supervisor is Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen, The Niels Bohr Institute, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ************************************************************************

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Electrical Engineering, Physics, Nanoscience, Photonics or Materials Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in AI-driven knowledge graphs and network models of plant stress responses
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational plant biology. The project is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093). The programme aims to make heat and drought resilience engineering in Nordic crops predictable by converting the plant literature and multi-omics data into evidence-backed predictions of gene function and stress regulation.

  Start date is expected to be 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Most plant genes remain functionally uncharacterised, and the knowledge that does exist is scattered across more than 200,000 articles. Our knowledge graph PlantConnectome has shown that large language models can extract this knowledge at scale; this project will build its successor and use it to predict gene function.

  You will:

   	
• Fine-tune open large language models (e.g. Llama-class models with QLoRA) on our existing, curated knowledge graph, and use the best checkpoint to extract entities, relationships and supporting evidence from >200,000 open-access plant articles spanning model species and crops 	
• Build a provenance-aware knowledge graph an order of magnitude larger than PlantConnectome, in which every edge is traceable to the sentence and experiment that supports it 	
• Predict new gene–GO associations by direct-neighbourhood reasoning (matching LLM-generated entity definitions to GO terms with embeddings and an LLM guardrail) and by path-based link prediction with graph neural networks, evaluated CAFA-style against held-out annotations 	
• Turn regulatory relationships in the graph into Boolean and related discrete network models of stress signalling, simulate them, and test their predictions against expression data generated in the group 	
• Distinguish well-supported from over-cited claims, and represent evidence quality and independence explicitly in the graph   The position is computational, but sits in a group that generates its own single-cell stress data and validates predictions in rapeseed, so your predictions will be tested.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, physics, mathematics or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with natural language processing, large language models, graph databases, network modelling or machine learning is an advantage. An interest in how plants actually work is essential; a formal background in plant biology is not.

  What we value  Coding experience is welcome but not required at entry – we teach it. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

   	
• questioning data rather than accepting it – asking what was measured, how, and against which expectation 	
• noticing anomalies and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting computational evidence to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are equally interested in candidates from biology who want to learn computation and candidates from computer science, physics or engineering who want to learn biology.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen.

jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in plant stress physiology and single-cell biology. The project is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093).

  Start date is expected to be 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Stress responses are usually measured in whole organs, which averages away the fact that different cell types respond differently, and sometimes in opposite directions. This project will resolve heat and drought responses at single-cell resolution in four major Nordic crops – the dicots rapeseed and potato and the monocots wheat and barley – and ask which regulatory programmes are conserved across them.

  You will design and carry out the stress experiments yourself: heat, drought and the two combined, sampled at early (3 h), middle (6 h) and late (2 days) stages, in leaves, roots and floral meristems. Single-cell RNA-seq and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) libraries are generated on the group’s 10x Genomics platform and sequenced by an external provider. You will then analyse the data yourself – we will train you in data science, so no prior programming experience is required. What we need from you at the start is the experimentalist’s judgment: how to grow, stress and sample plants so that the data can answer the question.

  Depending on your interests, the work may include:

   	
• Designing and running the stress experiments: growth conditions, stress intensities, time points, physiological read-outs and replication, so that the resulting data can actually answer the question 	
• Phenotyping and physiological characterisation of the stressed plants, and nuclei/cell isolation for single-cell sequencing 	
• Quality control, integration and cell-type annotation of single-cell atlases across stresses, organs and species 	
• Extending the group’s TEA-GCN method to single-cell data to infer cell-type- and stress-specific transcription factor–target relationships 	
• Linking transcription factors to cis-regulatory elements using ATAC-seq, known motifs and sequence-based deep learning 	
• Ranking regulatory edges by conservation across the four crops to obtain high-confidence networks, and comparing them with the group’s cross-species stress atlases   You will not be alone with the data: the grant also funds a computational postdoc who develops the multimodal integration methods alongside you, and the work draws on a collaboration with Prof. Ryan Lister (University of Western Australia) on multimodal single-cell methods and on stress-physiology expertise at PLEN Taastrup.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for an experimentalist: a candidate within the field(s) of plant physiology, plant molecular biology, agronomy or crop science, preferably with hands-on experience of growing plants and running stress or phenotyping experiments. Applicants can have a background from biology, plant sciences, agricultural sciences, biotechnology or a related discipline. What is required is the willingness to become fluent in analysing your own data.

  What we value  Programming experience is not required at entry – we teach it, and the training in data science is part of the position. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

• noticing anomalies in a growth chamber or a dataset and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting a measurement to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are looking for a plant experimentalist who wants to own the analysis of their own data, not hand it to someone else.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. The Centre for Medical Science and Technology Studies at the Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a 32 month postdoc in Medical Science and Technology Studies/Medical Anthropology. The position is available from February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The postdoc is available via the Carlsberg Foundation Semper Ardens Accelerate-funded project PATHWAYs of precision: AI-driven predictions in neurocognitive and mental illness | Carlsbergfondet.dk, and will employ ethnographic methods to explore the use of predictive Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare and its implications for contemporary medical practice.

   

  Project description

  We seek a highly motivated postdoc with a strong interest in ethnographic research on the social, ethical, and organizational implications of novel digital and data-intensive medical technologies. Specifically, the postdoc will investigate and theorize how predictive AI-based voice biomarker models for the identification and diagnosis of dementia establish new pathways for patient and personhood, professional practice, and healthcare delivery. The postdoc will conduct participant observation in clinical settings at hospitals, qualitative interviews with healthcare professionals, patients, and biomedical/bioinformatics scientists, as well as document analysis of policy papers and clinical guidelines related to AI in healthcare.

   

  Our group and research
 The postdoc will be based at the Centre for Medical Science and Technology Studies (MeST) at the Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. MeST is a vibrant, internationally recognized, and highly interdisciplinary research environment with scholars from public health, anthropology, sociology, history, psychology, medicine, and philosophy. United by a shared interest in how medical technologies shape and interact with humans and healthcare systems, MeST researchers explore a wide range of topics, with a particular—though not exclusive—focus on precision medicine and digital health. The center provides a stimulating intellectual setting, offering opportunities for collaboration, academic exchange, and methodological innovation.

   

  Principal Investigator is Associate Professor Iben Mundbjerg Gjødsbøl, e-mail: ibgj@sund.ku.dk, direct phone: 35337318. 

  Start:            February 15, 2027 

  Duration:     32 months

   

  Your job
 Your key tasks as a postdoc are:

   	
• Carrying through an independent ethnographic research project in collaboration with the research team,  	
• Participating in active research environments, including a stay with an international research team. 	
• Teaching and disseminating your knowledge 	
• Writing three peer-reviewed articles in high-ranking international journals on the grounds of your project    

  Profile

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic social scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• You have a PhD in anthropology, Science and Technology Studies, ethnology, public health, or sociology 	
• You are highly experienced in conducting ethnographic research in healthcare settings 	
• You have an active interest in medical anthropology/medical science and technology studies 	
• You are skilled in theorizing the use and implications of digital and AI-based predictive technologies in healthcare 	
• You demonstrate excellent written and oral command of English. 	
• You demonstrate excellent written and oral command of Danish. As fieldwork will be conducted in Danish clinical settings with Danish-speaking patients and healthcare professionals, fluency in Danish from the outset of the position is an absolute requirement. 	
• You are willing to work interdisciplinarily and collaboratively.
